problems.explain: Divide by √2: cos x = 1/√2 = √2/2. The reference angle is π/4, since cos π/4 = √2/2. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV: x = π/4 and x = 2π − π/4 = 7π/4. (Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV, so the partner is 2π minus the angle, not π minus it.) So x = π/4 and 7π/4.

prompt.v: Solve √2 sin x = −1 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

problems.text: solve radians: sqrt(2)*sin(x) = -1; options a: 1/4, 3/4 | b: 5/4 | c: 5/4, 7/4 | d: 3/4, 5/4
problems.explain: Divide by √2: sin x = −1/√2 = −√2/2. The reference angle is π/4, since sin π/4 = √2/2. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV: x = π + π/4 = 5π/4 and x = 2π − π/4 = 7π/4. (sin⁻¹(−√2/2) is −π/4, which is not between 0 and 2π: work from the reference angle instead.) So x = 5π/4 and 7π/4.

prompt.v: Solve √2 sin x = 1 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

problems.text: solve radians: sqrt(2)*sin(x) = 1; options a: 3/4, 7/4 | b: 1/4 | c: 5/4, 7/4 | d: 1/4, 3/4
problems.explain: Divide by √2: sin x = 1/√2 = √2/2. The reference angle is π/4, since sin π/4 = √2/2. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II: x = π/4 and x = π − π/4 = 3π/4. (sin⁻¹ gives only π/4; the partner in quadrant II, π minus it, is the one most often missed.) So x = π/4 and 3π/4.

prompt.v: Solve √3 tan x = 1 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

problems.text: solve radians: sqrt(3)*tan(x) = 1; options a: 1/6 | b: 1/6, 11/6 | c: 1/6, 7/6 | d: 5/6, 7/6
problems.explain: Divide by √3: tan x = 1/√3 = √3/3. The reference angle is π/6, since tan π/6 = √3/3. Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III: x = π/6 and x = π + π/6 = 7π/6. (Tangent repeats every π, so the second solution is π on from the first.) So x = π/6 and 7π/6.
